newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.

text.p: Singapore government bonds closed lower across the board in moderate trade following a slight hike in the interbank rate, dealers said on Wednesday.

"Bond prices were marked down slightly following a small hike in the interbank rate. Treasury bill rates were also slightly lower. Basically, the market is just correcting itself after the long holidays. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.05/98.10 compared with Tuesday's close of S$99.10/99.15 and September 2001 at S$98.05/98.10 against S$98.20/98.25.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 7/8 3/4 percent versus Tuesday's 5/8 1/2 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 0.60/0.55 percent against Tuesday's yield of 0.73/0.68 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.33/1.28 percent from 1.35/1.30 percent.
